shared_elements: human figure (schematic stick figures in A; a modelled human head in B)
rows of repeated short parallel strokes (crew-strokes on boats vs fluted headdress and hair combing)
repeated small round units (line of cup-marks vs rows of spiral curls)
justification: The only correspondences are wholly generic: both include human presence and fields of repeated small marks (a vertical line of dots and rows of crew-strokes in A, rows of curls and fluting in B), which any tradition could produce independently. A depicts a scattered scene of outlined boats with upturned prows, stick-figure people and cup-marks in a flat schematic idiom, while B depicts a single large, naturalistically modelled profile head with beard, ear and headdress — no shared motif, relationship or manner of depiction.
